name: lodash-iteratee-thisarg
behavioral_change: lodash v4.0.0 removed the `thisArg` parameter from iteration methods such as `_.every`, `_.map` and `_.each`. The signature and call form are unchanged and the third argument is silently ignored, so `this` inside the iteratee is no longer bound to the caller object as it was in v_old.
downstream_effect: In the downstream project, `ParseContext.prototype.parse` uses `_.every(['Function','Array','Object'], fn, this)` to classify a filter; after the upgrade `this.filter` inside `fn` is undefined, every branch is rejected, and parsing falls back to returning the filter function itself. The failure is a should assertion ("expected Function { name: 'foo' } to be 'bar'") pointing at test/Parser-test.js and library-internal frames, never mentioning lodash, thisArg or ParseContext.
reference_fix: The reference fix edits three iteratee calls in lib/ParseContext.js (around lines 25, 48 and 88), dropping the third `this` argument and binding the iteratee with `Function#bind` instead.
documented_in: The lodash Changelog for v4.0.0 (https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki/Changelog#v400), Compatibility Warnings section, states that `thisArg` params were removed and can be replaced with `_.bind`, `Function#bind` or arrow functions; the entry includes a before/after code block (`_.map(objects, callback, context)` in 3.10.1 versus `_.map(objects, _.bind(callback, context))` in 4.0.0), which shows the new code form.
failing_tests: Parser provides helper methods #parse runs htmlToJson.parse against the stored filter
Parser provides helper methods #request runs htmlToJson.request against the stored filter

no_summary_states.STATE-NEW: mocha 2.5.3 aborts the process right after printing Fatal AssertionError in STATE-NEW and never reaches the epilogue, so that state has no summary line. STATE-OLD and STATE-FIXED both report 20 passing; exit code 2 comes from a real assertion failure, not from a test run that failed to start.
